question: In chronic suppurative otitis media, a perforation in the pars flaccida (attic) region of the tympanic membrane is more likely to be associated with cholesteatoma and unsafe CSOM than a perforation in the pars tensa.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true and represents one of the most important clinical distinctions in ENT. Pars flaccida (attic) perforation = unsafe CSOM = cholesteatoma risk = refer for surgery. Pars tensa (central) perforation = safe CSOM = medical management first. The location of the perforation on otoscopy directly changes the management pathway.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This is a high-yield clinical distinction. Attic (pars flaccida) perforations are the hallmark of unsafe CSOM (cholesteatoma type), which carries the risk of erosive complications — ossicular destruction, lateral sinus thrombosis, meningitis. Pars tensa perforations (central) are associated with safe (tubotympanic) CSOM with mucopurulent discharge but without cholesteatoma.
